subject: VeloxCare: consumption signals, term options & renewal playbook
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Matthew Ross <matthew.ross@veloxcare.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 28 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: VeloxCare: initial consumption read + renewal check-in

Hi Matthew —

Quick primer ahead of the renewal window: we pulled a short consumption and perf read for VeloxCare (attached CSV + token/latency breakdown). High-level signals:

- Net token consumption (last 90d): ~86M tokens/month, +28% vs prior quarter (main tracer: user-facing summarization pipeline).
- Median p95 latency for chat endpoints: 210ms (hosted), spikes to 420ms during peak 11:00–13:00 PT.
- Cost per 1M tokens (billable): baseline $9.2k current effective unit after usage-based credits.

We see predictable seasonality and a clear runway to benefit from a modest committed headroom/term shift (helps cost predictability + burst credits). To make the renewal conversation actionable, would you be open to a 30-minute sync next week to review a short playbook (tiers, headroom, optional SLA uplift and burst credits)?

I attached: veloxcare_usage_nov2027.csv and latency_token_breakdown.xlsx.

Proposed next steps if you’re open:
- Quick align call (30m) to confirm hotspot endpoints and acceptable SLOs
- We’ll prepare 1-page term options (12/24/36mo) with estimated unit economics and burst credit allocation

Available: Tue 11/30 10:00–11:30 PT or Wed 12/1 08:00–11:00 PT. Which works best?

Thanks —
Rachel Kim
Account Exec, Renewals & Expansion
Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.ai

--
Attachment stubs:
- veloxcare_usage_nov2027.csv (CSV)
- latency_token_breakdown.xlsx (XLSX)
From: Matthew Ross <matthew.ross@veloxcare.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2027 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: VeloxCare: initial consumption read + renewal check-in

Thanks Rachel — this looks useful. A couple quick Qs before we schedule:

1) Can you break down the ~86M tokens by product (in-app summaries vs batch ingestion)? We want to make sure this growth is concentrated in the in-app paths.
2) Our procurement lead will want to see the delta in effective unit cost if we move to a 24-month commit vs staying month-to-month. Any estimate you can send ahead of the call?

Also can you confirm whether the SLA uplift is Limited to Dedicated pools or if hosted customers can purchase the higher SLO bundle? We may need the lower latency envelope for a pilot.

I can do Wed 12/1 at 09:00 PT. Looping procurement once we have the draft.

Matt
Matthew Ross
Head of Engineering, VeloxCare
matthew.ross@veloxcare.com
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2027 12:05:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: VeloxCare: initial consumption read + renewal check-in (internal)

Ben / Monica — forwarding Matt's reply. Quick internal notes (do not share in this form):

- Product mix: the CSV tags show ~63% in-app (realtime chat/summarization) and ~37% batch ingestion (ETL summarizers). Growth is primarily in-app.
- Economics: rough estimate moving to a 24mo commit with +20% headroom (to cover projected 12–18mo growth) yields ~18% reduction in effective unit cost vs current month-to-month blended pricing. That includes a one-time onboarding credit and 40k burst credits we can throw in for pilot smoothing.
- SLA: Dedicated pools provide the firm p95 < 200ms SLO; hosted customers can purchase the SLO uplift (higher priority routing + burst capacity) but p95 guarantee is only SLA-backed on Dedicated. For pilot we can offer a hosted SLO uplift + 30k burst credits to minimize migration friction.

Ask: can you draft two short-term proposals: (A) 24mo commit with 20% headroom + 18% effective unit reduction + 40k burst credits; (B) 12mo commit with 10% headroom + 8% reduction + 20k burst credits. Include a simple ROI table showing months-to-payback assuming current growth curve. I can own the call.

Thanks —
Rachel

--
[Internal note: keep final pricing sensitive until we have procurement on the call; mark any aggressive concession as NG for Legal unless ACC approves.]
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Matthew Ross <matthew.ross@veloxcare.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Nov 2027 15:45:00 -0800
Subject: VeloxCare renewal options + short ROI playbook (proposal attached)

Hi Matt — following up with the two short options we discussed. Attached: veloxcare_renewal_proposal_2027-12.pdf (1-page term options) and a supporting ROI extract. TL;DR: 24mo with 20% headroom gives the best blended unit economics and preserves runway for your product ramp; 12mo is lower commitment but less unit savings.

Summary (numbers are illustrative; final will be in the DocuSign package):
- Option A (24mo, +20% headroom): ~18% reduction in effective unit price; includes 40k burst credits; SLA uplift available (hosted premium) or Dedicated migration path with 99.95% SLA (optional). Estimated monthly spend at current run-rate: $79k/mo.
- Option B (12mo, +10% headroom): ~8% reduction; includes 20k burst credits; estimated $87k/mo at current run-rate.

Proposed next steps:
1) 30-min alignment call Wed 12/1 09:00 PT (confirmed) to run through the packet and procurement asks.
2) We’ll send a formal DocuSign with option A prefilled and option B as alternate within 24 hours after call.
3) If you want Legal/Security on the call, add them and we’ll loop Monica.

Links: HubSpot deal (https://app.hubspot.com/deal/87932) and a staging DocuSign we’ll use after sign-off.

Thanks, looking forward to the call.

—
Rachel Kim
Account Exec, Renewals & Expansion
Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0132
rachel.kim@redwood.ai

Quick ask ahead of the call: can you attach the 24mo cost schedule line-items (monthly unit price, credits, SLA uplift cost) in spreadsheet form so our procurement can do a quick internal review? Also if you have a one-page migration checklist for Dedicated migration (risk/effort) that will help the pilot discussion.

See you on the call —
Matt
